title: Redwood structured output + function calling demo - Lumen Retail
summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood's JSON structured output and function/tool calling. Demo covered schema enforcement, validation, console UI, and Optimize recommendations. Customer raised security, data residency, and latency/cost tradeoffs; agreed to POC benchmarks and security docs exchange.
next_steps: Alex to share pricing sheet and POC proposal (by 2026-01-19)
Priya to run sample benchmark with customer dataset and share results (by 2026-01-23)
Alex to share SOC2 / security package and VPC deployment checklist (by 2026-01-18)
Schedule technical POC kickoff (tentative week of 2026-01-26)
action_items: Alex Torres | Send pricing + POC proposal | due 2026-01-19
Priya Singh | Run latency/cost benchmark on sample payloads and produce spreadsheet | due 2026-01-23
Samir Rao (Lumen) | Provide sample API payloads & security contacts | due 2026-01-16
Jordan Kim | Prepare onboarding checklist & dedicated capacity options | due 2026-01-20
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Torres: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, i'll be the AE on this call, with Priya our solutions engineer. uh quick roll call?
[00:12] Chris Patel: Chris here, CTO, Maya and Jason are on from product and ML. Samir from security is also here.
[00:20] Alex Torres: awesome, thanks. today's focus is structured output and function calling — JSON mode, schemas, and guardrails — and how that looks in the API and the console, plus some Optimize tips.
[00:35] Priya Singh: quick agenda: show JSON mode with a schema, demonstrate function calling / tool integrations, show console validation and fallback behaviors, and talk about performance and cost with Optimize.
[00:50] Maya Chen: sounds good, specifically want to see how strict the schema enforcement is and how we can avoid hallucinations when producing ecomm product metadata.
[01:05] Priya Singh: great, we'll use a product ingestion example—title, description, price, category, stock, and nested attributes—and show how Redwood enforces types and returns structured JSON.
[01:20] Alex Torres: quick qualification: where are you running inference today? cloud? self-hosted?
[01:28] Jason Lee: currently using a mix — some models via managed endpoints on vendor A, and some on prem for sensitive data. looking to standardize inference and reduce cost.
[01:40] Alex Torres: got it. budget/timeline?
[01:42] Chris Patel: evaluating providers now, timeline is next 8-12 weeks for a POC, then procurement. cost is important but security is blocking for certain catalogs.
[01:55] Priya Singh: ok thanks. i'll share my screen and start the demo — bear with me if the layout looks a bit different, screen share lag.
[02:10] [02:10] Priya Singh: (screen) here's the API call, schema defined inline, we set required fields and types, also a strict mode flag so model outputs that don't match the schema are either rejected or mapped to closest fields.
[02:30] [02:30] Priya Singh: example payload — prompt + schema — sending to our hosted endpoint with JSON mode. note the response includes a top-level "structured" object and a confidence vector per field.
[02:48] Maya Chen: when you say confidence vector, is that per-token or per-field?
[02:53] Priya Singh: per-field scoring — it's computed by the runtime based on token alignments and our post-run heuristics, not an absolute probability but useful for thresholds.
[03:10] Chris Patel: what about required nested arrays? sometimes product attributes are arrays with variable length. will strict mode break if length mismatches?
[03:20] Priya Singh: we support flexible arrays, you can set minItems/maxItems and use allowExtraItems flag. strict mode focuses on types and required presence; there are policies for trimming or filling defaults.
[03:36] Alex Torres: another feature — function calling integration. you can register a function in the model catalog that maps to your inventory API, Redwood will emit a canonical function call object when intent is detected.
[03:50] [03:50] Priya Singh: demo time — show a function call sample: model suggests calling update_inventory(product_id, delta, location). the SDK automatically translates that into an outbound API call if enabled, otherwise returns a function_call object for your app to handle.
[04:08] Maya Chen: is there retries/batching built in for those outbound calls?
[04:13] Priya Singh: Redwood handles retries, idempotency tokens, and you can enable built-in batching for high-throughput pipelines. batching has tunable latencies to balance cost.
[04:30] Samir Rao: security question: when function calls trigger outbound webhooks, does Redwood inspect payloads or is that passthrough?
[04:37] Priya Singh: by default it's passthrough, but you can enable policy-based validation on outbound calls and route through your VPC connector in Private deployments. we also support signing and HMAC verification on callbacks.
[04:55] [04:55] Alex Torres: switching to the console — here's the structured-output panel, you can test schemas interactively, see sample mismatches highlighted, and toggle strict vs permissive modes.
[05:12] [05:12] Priya Singh: i'll intentionally send a malformed response to show guardrails — notice the UI flags an invalid price format (string instead of number) and suggests auto-coercion if you opt in.
[05:30] Jason Lee: can we add custom validation rules, like price must be > 0 and currency must be in our allowed set?
[05:36] Priya Singh: yes, you can add custom validators and even plug in a webhook validator that calls your service to run domain-specific checks.
[05:50] Alex Torres: on the API side, you can also set post-processing transforms which are small, deterministic mapping steps—useful for cleanups before writing to your DB.
[06:05] Maya Chen: how do you handle hallucinations where model invents skus or attributes?
[06:12] Priya Singh: multiple layers: schema enforcement rejects invalid types/unknown fields; function calling + inventory lookup verifies existence; cached prefix matching reduces free-text inventing; and Optimize suggests quantization/model settings that reduce hallucination for your workload.
[06:33] [06:33] Priya Singh: demoing function calling with inventory lookup: model emits function call, Redwood either executes (if you set execute=true) or returns call object. we intentionally disabled exec and looked at the call payload — you can inspect arguments and confidence per arg.
[06:55] Chris Patel: what happens if the function fails? do you get a fallback plan?
[07:00] Priya Singh: yes you can configure fallback strategies: retry, call alternate function, or return a structured error object to the app. can even define canary paths.
[07:15] Alex Torres: performance — Priya will show latency numbers and how Optimize recommends batching/quantization pairs.
[07:24] [07:24] Priya Singh: here's a benchmark for a 512-token average product description with an LLM family we host; median latency on hosted baseline is ~180ms per request with small-quantized model, throughput increases with batching but tail latency rises.
[07:40] Priya Singh: Optimize suggests enabling KV caching for repeated prefix prompts (title/brand) and a 4-bit quant profile for cost reduction with a small hit to peak generation quality that is fine for metadata.
[08:00] Jason Lee: can we pin model versions during rollout? we need deterministic outputs for audits.
[08:07] Alex Torres: yes, pin model versions and use rollout policies—canary at 10%, A/B, or gradual increase. console stores evals per prompt set so you can compare outputs.
[08:22] Samir Rao: security again — does Redwood store request/response payloads by default? retention policies?
[08:30] Priya Singh: default retention is 30 days, enterprise plans can extend or disable logging; Private deployment keeps logs in your VPC and integrates with your KMS/HSM for key management. audit logs are supported.
[08:44] Chris Patel: good. we need SOC2 docs and details on encryption in transit and at rest.
[08:49] Alex Torres: noted — we'll send the security package after the call.
[08:55] [08:55] Priya Singh: back to demo — showing error cases: model returns unexpected field, console shows a transform rule you can set to map or drop unknown fields. you can also trigger a human-in-the-loop approval flow for certain critical categories.
[09:15] Maya Chen: HIL sounds useful for catalog updates that change pricing.
[09:20] Priya Singh: yep, and you can set thresholds based on confidence vectors; below threshold triggers review.
[09:34] [09:34] Alex Torres: talk about private vs hosted: Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and isolated pools; Private gives VPC/on-prem control. which would you likely prefer for the POC?
[09:48] Chris Patel: likely hosted for initial POC, but private for production for certain catalogs.
[09:55] Alex Torres: that aligns with many customers — quick POC hosted, then migrate sensitive workloads to Private with a hybrid split.
[10:06] Priya Singh: showing the SDK pattern now — simple call in node/python. function calling is a param on the request. here's schema JSON and strict:true flag.
[10:22] [10:22] Priya Singh: we run a live request: response returns structured JSON matching schema, note we also log a field-level confidence array: "price": {"value": 19.99, "confidence": 0.87}.
[10:40] Maya Chen: is confidence persisted per-request for analytics?
[10:44] Priya Singh: yes, you can store field-level metrics and create alerts on regressions via eval sets.
[10:55] Jason Lee: support for multiple locales/currencies? we operate EU and US catalogs.
[11:01] Priya Singh: supported — locale-aware tokenization and you can pass a locale param to prefer certain formats; Optimize will recommend model/quantization per-region.
[11:14] Samir Rao: data residency? EU-only storage?
[11:18] Alex Torres: enterprise/private deployments can ensure EU-only hosting and control plane placement; hosted API has regional endpoints but enterprise contracts can specify residency.
[11:30] [11:30] Priya Singh: moving to tool calling — we integrate with partner tools and internal APIs. demoing a tool chain where model extracts an order and calls a combine-order API.
[11:48] Priya Singh: the console shows the full call trace and you can redact sensitive fields before storing. we also show a replay tool to debug when calls fail.
[12:02] Maya Chen: can we have granular RBAC so only certain roles can enable execute=true?
[12:07] Alex Torres: yes RBAC and SSO controls available; you can lock dangerous settings behind roles.
[12:15] [12:15] Priya Singh: showing Optimize recommendations now — for this workload it suggests enabling batching at 50ms window, 4-bit quant, and enabling prefix KV cache for sku/title. estimated cost reduction ~35% with <5% hit to certain free-text descriptions.
[12:40] Jason Lee: curious about regression detection — we need to ensure product descriptions don't degrade.
[12:46] Priya Singh: Redwood's evals let you run prompt sets and compare outputs across model versions and quantization profiles; you can alert on delta in BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity or custom metrics.
[13:00] Chris Patel: we will want automated alerts tied to our QA prompts.
[13:04] Alex Torres: ok, we'll include guidance on creating eval sets in the security/package docs.
[13:12] [13:12] Priya Singh: quick note on latency: for strict real-time use cases, Dedicated + smaller models with KV cache provide low tail latency. hosted multi-tenant is fine for many use cases but tail can be variable.
[13:30] Samir Rao: any certifications? SOC2, ISO?
[13:33] Alex Torres: Redwood has SOC2 Type II; we'll share certs.
[13:38] Maya Chen: about price — can you share a sample pricing for hosted vs dedicated?
[13:42] Alex Torres: we'll send a pricing sheet; committed Dedicated discounts available and we show examples of per-request costs in the proposal.
[13:52] [13:52] Priya Singh: demoing schema evolution — how to deploy new schema versions without breaking production: we show staged rollout and a compatibility checker that flags incompatible changes.
[14:10] Jason Lee: nice. do you support mapping old fields to new ones automatically?
[14:15] Priya Singh: yes via transform rules and deprecation warnings in the console.
[14:24] Chris Patel: what about auditability — we need full trace for regulatory purposes.
[14:29] Priya Singh: request/response traces, function call traces, and execution logs are stored and can be forwarded to your SIEM; private deployments can keep everything in your logging stack.
[14:40] [14:40] Alex Torres: real customer example: a retail customer reduced manual QA by 60% using strict schemas + HIL for price changes, saved ~30% inference cost after Optimize recommendations.
[14:55] Maya Chen: that line on QA reduction is interesting.
[15:00] Priya Singh: showing a failure example where model returns extra attributes; console transform drops unknowns and flags for review, we also show a replay of the exact tokens that led to mis-alignment.
[15:18] Jason Lee: is token-level tracing available to customers?
[15:22] Priya Singh: yes, with anonymization options; we provide token-level traces in debug mode and aggregated stats in normal ops.
[15:34] Samir Rao: encryption keys — do customers manage keys?
[15:37] Alex Torres: enterprise/private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integration.
[15:42] [15:42] Priya Singh: walking through the POC checklist: define success metrics, provide sample payloads, choose models and accuracy thresholds, pick deployment mode, schedule benching.
[15:56] Maya Chen: for success metrics we'll define per-field precision/recall and allowed latency windows.
[16:03] Alex Torres: perfect. Priya, can you run a quick smoke test with a sample payload Chris provided earlier?
[16:10] Priya Singh: yes loading sample now, sending request — response comes back: structured JSON with a minor mismatch on "stock" datatype. console suggests coercion.
[16:28] Maya Chen: we prefer strict rejects, then a human review. can that be a configurable org policy?
[16:35] Priya Singh: yes, policy layer is org-scoped and role-based.
[16:42] [16:42] Chris Patel: any limitations on the number of registered functions or rate limits for function execution?
[16:50] Priya Singh: there are soft limits per account but we can increase for enterprise; outbound function execution throughput is tied to your capacity plan.
[17:02] Jason Lee: curious about cost of running many small function calls vs bundling into one call that handles batch updates.
[17:10] Priya Singh: Optimize can recommend batching patterns and also suggest model variants that are cheaper for bulk ops. bundling reduces round trips but may increase complexity.
[17:24] [17:24] Alex Torres: switching to questions from Samir on compliance controls for exposure of PII in logs.
[17:33] Samir Rao: we need PII redaction before storage for certain datasets.
[17:38] Priya Singh: Redwood supports redact-on-ingest rules and custom redaction hooks; in Private you can fully control retention and redaction.
[17:50] Chris Patel: good, please include redaction settings in the security docs.
[17:55] Alex Torres: will do.
[18:00] [18:00] Priya Singh: live demo of a fallback chain — model fails to call inventory service, fallback triggers cached view and returns structured response with note "inventory_status": "fallback_cache".
[18:18] Maya Chen: how do we surface fallback to product managers?
[18:22] Priya Singh: console flags and alerting; you can also send events to your webhook for downstream analytics.
[18:34] Jason Lee: are there SDKs for Java and Go?
[18:38] Alex Torres: yes official SDKs for JS/Python/Go/Java, plus REST.
[18:44] [18:44] Priya Singh: demoing schema drafts and using the console's schema validator. showing an incompatible change detection when I rename a field.
[18:58] Maya Chen: can we auto-generate schema from sample data?
[19:02] Priya Singh: yes the console can infer a draft schema from sample payloads which is handy to start.
[19:14] Chris Patel: network-wise, for Private deployment what are the requirements?
[19:18] Priya Singh: typical: VPC peering, egress rules for telemetry (if enabled), optionally you can keep control plane in Redwood and data plane in your VPC. we'll share the checklist.
[19:30] Alex Torres: quick pause — any blockers to moving forward?
[19:33] Chris Patel: none huge, just need security review and pricing clarity.
[19:38] Alex Torres: great. Priya, final demo piece?
[19:42] Priya Singh: final — a tool chain example with function calling plus post-processing transforms and an eval showing rollout comparison between model v1 and v1-quant4. the console highlights a small semantic drop for long-form descriptions but metadata fields remain stable.
[20:05] Maya Chen: what's the recommended model family for metadata-only use cases?
[20:10] Priya Singh: smaller LLMs with strong instruction tuning often suffice; Optimize will pick a candidate set and run sample evals to recommend the best cost/quality tradeoff.
[20:22] Jason Lee: ok how long to spin up a POC?
[20:25] Alex Torres: typical hosted POC can start within a week after paperwork; Private takes longer for network setup.
[20:34] Samir Rao: procurement question — do you support standard enterprise NDAs?
[20:38] Alex Torres: yes we can sign our standard MSA and integrate SSO, just send your legal contacts.
[20:44] [20:44] Priya Singh: quick note about observability — token-level cost breakdown, route-level latency, and model-level cost dashboards. you can allocate costs per-product line.
[20:58] Maya Chen: nice. any rate limits on eval runs?
[21:02] Priya Singh: small limits by default but enterprise POCs can bump.
[21:10] Alex Torres: alright wrapping up demo, time for recap and next steps.
[21:16] Alex Torres: recap: we showed structured-output JSON mode, schema enforcement, function/tool calling, console guardrails, and Optimize recommendations.
[21:26] Chris Patel: thanks — helpful. next steps: we'll share sample payloads and Samir will review security docs.
[21:34] Alex Torres: action items captured — Alex to send pricing and security docs, Priya to run bench on sample payloads, Jordan to prep onboarding notes.
[21:45] Maya Chen: one more question — do you provide an SLA for hosted endpoints during POC?
[21:50] Alex Torres: for POC we provide best-effort; dedicated plans have formal SLA.
[21:56] Chris Patel: acceptable for now.
[22:00] [22:00] Alex Torres: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the proposal and a calendar invite for a POC kickoff.
[22:08] Jason Lee: thanks all.
[22:12] Samir Rao: thanks.
[22:15] Maya Chen: bye.
[22:20] Alex Torres: bye.

Note: transcript contains occasional transcription errors and speaker attribution inconsistencies typical of Fireflies exports.
